# AI Governance Programme Lead / Manager

> The dedicated, mostly non-coding governance career: runs the AI inventory, risk method, committees and conformity with the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Governance, Risk & Assurance | Security, safety and governance (plane) | Verified (V) | #17 of 24 | #16 of 24 · band B · Monte Carlo rank 17 (P10–P90 14–20) | E2 Governance & assurance |

## What you need

- **Must (headline):** GRC & risk assessment, EU AI Act / NIST AI RMF / ISO 42001, Stakeholder communication, AI inventory & risk register.
- **Important (headline):** Sector rules (SR 26-2, LL144, DPDP), Content provenance (EU AI Act Art. 50), Privacy law & DPO duties, Observability (OpenTelemetry traces, metrics), Python/SQL (notebook level), AI operating model & governance boards.
- **Full inventory:** 58 skills (Must 6 · Important 21 · Should 19 · Optional 12), each with its evidence and posting keywords: [ai-governance-lead.md](../../03-skills-and-tech/inventories/ai-governance-lead.md).
- **Prerequisites:** About 5 years in GRC, privacy, audit or security; domain certifications first (CIPP/CIPM, CISSP/CISA/CRISC); AIGP optional [B · T0-15]
- **Credentials (tie-breakers, not skills):** IAPP Artificial Intelligence Governance Professional (AIGP) (Optional: optional; domain certifications come first); IAPP CIPP (privacy law, regional variants) (Optional: privacy-law route); IAPP CIPM (privacy programme management) (Optional: privacy-programme route); ISC2 CISSP (Optional: security route); ISACA CISA (Optional: audit route); ISACA CRISC (Optional: IT-risk route). Whether one is worth it: [credential ROI](../../04-certifications/credential-roi.md).
- What to learn first and what to drop across roles: [skills radar](../../03-skills-and-tech/skills-radar.md); in what order: [learning roadmaps](../../03-skills-and-tech/learning-roadmaps.md).

## How to prove it

- **What the evidence asks for:** An AI inventory, risk register and governance playbook mapped to the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001
- **Project archetypes that cover the most of its Must and Important skills** (Grade M): [P13 AI governance packet: inventory, risk register, framework mapping](../../05-portfolio/project-archetypes.md#p13) (62%); [P19 Model-validation / bias-audit report](../../05-portfolio/project-archetypes.md#p19) (29%); [P20 Responsible-AI compliance packet with runtime guardrails](../../05-portfolio/project-archetypes.md#p20) (21%). One project rarely covers a role; the [job-search strategy](../../06-job-search/job-search-strategy.md#the-constraints-that-bind-first) computes the smallest sets that do.
- How verifiable the proof must be, and what to publish: [proof-of-work standards](../../05-portfolio/proof-of-work-standards.md).

## How you are interviewed

- **Track: Governance.** It tests a scoping or solutions round, and fluency in the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001. Source: T1-03, T0-14 (first collected in the role catalog §8.2; this file is the owner).
- **Practise:** the [governance prep pack](../../08-interviewing/prep-packs.md#governance-pack), plus the behavioural and coding packs.
- Classify the loop first, then prepare by round: [interview loops](../../08-interviewing/interview-loops.md).

## Résumé

- **Variant:** E2 Governance & assurance (AI Product, Governance & Assurance); headline pattern: "AI Governance Lead: EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001". How to tailor it: [résumé strategy](../../06-job-search/resume-strategy.md).
- **Keywords to mirror, only when true:** AI governance, EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, risk management, compliance, privacy; Axial: observability/monitoring 42.3%, Python 27.1%
- **Leave out or reframe:** Listing AIGP as your main credential (domain certifications come first)
